Fetch a URL to disk with an Internet Archive fallback (C++/libcurl)

Source: R/fetch_native.R
blfetch.Rd

The shared data-fetch foundation of the morie ecosystem. Downloads url to dest; if the live download fails (404, network), it retries the Wayback Machine snapshot – so a rotated or removed source file (CIHI, open-data portals) stays retrievable. Backed by the package's C++ kernel rmbl_fetch_with_fallback (libcurl), which rmorie and morie share through LinkingTo. The return value says which source served the file, so a report can note that it used an archived copy.

Usage

blfetch(url, dest, wb = "", tmout = 120L)

Arguments

url

Live source URL, a single https string.

dest

Destination file path, a single string; its directory must exist.

wb

Optional explicit Wayback snapshot URL, a string. "" (default) or NULL auto-resolves one via wbsnpurl's API when the live download fails.

tmout

Per-request timeout in seconds, a positive whole number (default 120).

Value

Invisibly, "live" or "wayback": the source that served the file. Throws on total failure.

Details

Before any network use the arguments are checked: url must be one https URL to a public host (plain http only when the option rmoriebricklayer.allowhttp is TRUE; loopback, private, link-local and metadata addresses are refused), the directory of dest must exist and be writable, and tmout must be at least one second. The compiled layer then resolves the host, pins the connection to the checked addresses and re-checks every redirect.

If the live download fails, the fallback is the wb URL when given, else a snapshot looked up through the Wayback availability API (as wbsnpnat() does). dest is overwritten. A spinner is drawn on stderr while waiting, unless options(morie.quiet = TRUE).

Errors: invalid arguments as above; and, when both sources fail, an error saying whether the live URL could not be reached or answered an HTTP status, and whether the Wayback Machine had no snapshot or its copy could not be downloaded.

Examples

# Inputs are validated before any network access:
try(blfetch("", tempfile()))          # empty url -> error
#> Error : `url` must be one non-empty URL string
try(blfetch("ftp://example.org/data.csv", tempfile()))
#> Error : blfetch: 'ftp://example.org/data.csv' is not an http(s) URL
try(blfetch("https://127.0.0.1/data.csv", tempfile()))
#> Error : url points at a local or private address ('https://127.0.0.1/data.csv'): refused (a local or private address (127.0.0.1))
try(blfetch("https://example.org/data.csv",
                     file.path(tempdir(), "no-such-dir", "data.csv")))
#> Error : blfetch: cannot write /tmp/RtmpOjkl2Y/no-such-dir/data.csv (its directory does not exist)
if (FALSE) { # interactive()
# needs the network
dst <- tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx")

# Live download; auto-resolves a Wayback snapshot only if the live URL fails.
blfetch(
  paste0(
    "https://www.cihi.ca/sites/default/files/document/",
    "hospital-beds-2024-2025-data-tables-en.xlsx"
  ),
  dst
)

# Pin an explicit Wayback snapshot to fall back to, and a shorter timeout.
blfetch(
  "https://example.org/rotated-file.csv",
  tempfile(fileext = ".csv"),
  wb = paste0(
    "https://web.archive.org/web/2024id_/https://example.org/rotated-fil",
    "e.csv"
  ),
  tmout = 60
)

# The return value tells you which source served the file.
status <- blfetch("https://cloud.r-project.org/", tempfile())
status # "live" or "wayback"
}
